claims.text: Both Scientific Naturalism and Biblical Theism rest on unprovable foundational axioms — causal closure of the physical for science, divine aseity and revelation for theology.
claims.reviewer_notes: Central thesis of the chapter; explicitly stated and repeated. Load-bearing for the entire series.

claims.text: Science requires ten presuppositions it cannot validate with its own method — from the existence of the external world to the adequacy of mathematics to the value of honesty.
claims.reviewer_notes: Explicitly enumerated and attributed to Hugh Gauch. Core to the argument that science rests on unprovable axioms.

claims.text: Both systems exhibit structural circularity: science uses induction to validate induction; theology uses Scripture to validate Scripture. Both require an ultimate starting point that cannot be externally validated.
claims.reviewer_notes: Directly argued with historical references (Hume, Calvin). Central to leveling the playing field.

claims.text: The question is not 'faith versus evidence' but which foundational commitment accounts for more of what we actually observe.
claims.reviewer_notes: Framing claim; not directly evidenced but logically follows from the preceding. Sets up the series' evaluative approach.

claims.text: The foundational axiom of science — the natural world is causally closed — rules out the supernatural before it starts, not because it's been disproven, but because allowing it would break the method.
claims.reviewer_notes: Strong claim about methodological naturalism; plausible but could be challenged by philosophers of science who distinguish methodological from metaphysical naturalism. Overreached in its phrasing.

claims.text: The foundational axiom of theology — God is self-existent and has revealed himself — provides a pre-established harmony between the knower and the known that explains why science works.
claims.reviewer_notes: Theological claim; referenced but not deeply argued here. Sets up a later argument about the intelligibility of the universe.

claims.text: Neither side has won the argument before it started; the field is level, and the series will run the evidence in both directions.
claims.reviewer_notes: Explicitly stated in the closing paragraphs. Sets the agenda for the rest of the series.
